title: Re-enable allowAdditionalProperties:false once strata ships the inheritance fix
description:
schemas/strata.config.json leaves jsonSchema.allowAdditionalProperties at
its default (true) because setting it to false silently dropped struct
inheritance from the emitted JSON Schema on strata-cli 0.7.0 -- Contract
emitted with 5 of its 15 properties, valid-looking and wrong in both
directions.

Fix submitted upstream: strata-lang/strata PR #289. Once a strata release
carries it, flip the option back on and remove the workaround prose.

## Revisit every one of these together

- schemas/strata.config.json -- add "allowAdditionalProperties": false
  under jsonSchema, then run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
- schemas/README.md -- the whole "Known gap: undeclared keys are not
  rejected" section (currently the tail of the file) is deleted, not
  edited. Its two consequences bullets go with it.
- docs/adrs/ADR-016-strata-for-schema-and-model-generation.md -- the
  Consequences Negative bullet "Undeclared keys in specs.toml are not
  rejected by the schema" is removed. Note ADR-016 may be `active` by
  then; amend rather than rewrite, and bump updated_at.
- docs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md -- the guarantee that an
  undeclared key is reported becomes enforceable by the schema itself.
  The CLI still needs its own detection for the span, so the contract
  text likely stands; confirm rather than assume.
- scripts/validate-corpus.py -- will begin rejecting misspelled keys with
  no code change. Verify the corpus still passes before pushing; a
  document carrying an undeclared frontmatter key becomes a CI failure.
- cli/core/schema/*.json -- regenerated artifacts, committed.

## Verification

scripts/validate-corpus.py must stay green, and a deliberately misspelled
key in specs.toml must start failing it (it does not today -- that is the
gap). Confirm inheritance survives by checking that Contract in
cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json still reaches all 15 properties.

title: triage-rfc: check a proposal's extent and sufficiency before adopting (RFC P1)
description:
## Problem

The `triage-rfc` skill verifies that an RFC's quoted evidence EXISTS in
the tree, but never that the evidence is COMPLETE, nor that the proposed
change covers the evidence it cites. Every existing check points at
existence only:

- `.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:270` anti-pattern row: "Adopting
  on plausibility without verifying the quoted evidence" — checks the
  quote is really there.
- `SKILL.md:111` adopt-now criteria: "concrete change, verbatim
  evidence, small blast radius" — none is an extent check.
- `SKILL.md:221` verify bullet: "Re-read each file you changed" —
  scoped to files that DID change, so a file that should have changed
  and did not is outside it by construction.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

EXTENT. RFC 0007 P1 cited four occurrences of retired `@` notation in
three templates. The real count was six in five files:

    $ grep -rn '@<' plugin/skills/
    .../module-blueprint-template.md:317
    .../container-blueprint-template.md:323
    .../component-blueprint-template.md:193
    .../contract-template.md:108
    .../contract-template.md:202
    .../system-blueprint-template.md:219

`component-blueprint-template.md:193` and
`system-blueprint-template.md:219` were never cited — the authoring run
that produced the RFC never opened those two files. The sweep happened
only because that RFC's author wrote "Triage should also sweep the
remaining templates" into the proposal body. Nothing in the skill asks
for it. Adopting P1 as cited would have left two templates emitting
prohibited syntax while the Resolution recorded the class as fixed —
the exact outcome `SKILL.md:223` warns against ("A half-applied
adoption is worse than a deferral, because the Resolution will claim it
landed").

SUFFICIENCY. RFC 0007 P2's proposed text told the reader to assign "a
jsdom `window` and `document` onto `globalThis`". That same RFC's
finding 2 states six globals were needed: `window`, `document`,
`navigator`, `Element`, `HTMLElement`, `SVGElement`. The proposed fix
was inconsistent with the evidence in its own document; adopting it
verbatim would have shipped guidance that still fails.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P1 (severity blocker, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Insert after step 3's classification list (after the
`already-implemented` bullet, before the line `4. **Present the
recommendation and STOP for approval.**`), at 3-space indent to match
the surrounding step body:

   Before classifying a proposal **adopt-now**, run two checks its
   author could not have run. Both are triage's, and each has a
   recorded outcome:

   - **Extent.** WHEN the evidence cites occurrences of a repeatable
     pattern — a syntax, a phrase, a defect class — enumerate that
     pattern across the whole surface before adopting. A cited list is
     a sample from one run's path, not a census: the reporting run only
     opened the files its task required. Put the enumerating command
     and its result in the Resolution.
   - **Sufficiency.** Read the proposed Change against the finding it
     cites. WHEN the change resolves less than its own evidence
     describes, widen it and adopt with refinement.

   Failing either check does not sink a proposal — it resizes it. A
   proposal whose extent was understated is adopted with refinement
   over the full set, not rejected.

Then append this row to the Anti-Patterns table at the end of the file
(table cells are exempt from the 80-column rule):

| Treating a proposal's cited occurrences as the complete set | The RFC lists what its run touched; a defect class usually reaches files that run never opened, and the Resolution then records as fixed a class that is still live |

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead — agent-plugins bead for P5
owns the single 1.3 -> 1.4 bump and is last in this chain.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 3 carries an Extent check and a Sufficiency check, inserted after the already-implemented bullet
- [ ] The Anti-Patterns table has a row about treating cited occurrences as the complete set
- [ ] Every line added outside a table row is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: standard. tier_reason: the wording is supplied verbatim, but it lands in two separate regions of the file (step 3 body and the trailing table) and the table row must be recognised as width-exempt while the prose is not. No C4 component is affected; this file is a skill, not a documented container or module.
close_reason: Step 3 gained Extent and Sufficiency checks; Anti-Patterns gained the cited-occurrences row. Version bump left to agent-plugins-905 per the chain.

metadata.tier_reason: wording supplied verbatim, but lands in two separate regions (step 3 body and the trailing Anti-Patterns table) and the table row is width-exempt while the prose is not

title: Feature blueprint for the spec CLI, then groom, then bead bonanza
description:
The stated goal of the spec-validation-cli work: build up the foundation needed to produce a great feature blueprint, groom it, and run a bead bonanza against it.

The foundation now in place: FRD-spec-validation-cli (approved), ADR-015 Go (approved), container-spec-cli, module-document-core, module-spec-profile (all approved), contract-specs-configuration and testing-standards (approved with amendments applied).

Still blocking: the four ADRs filed alongside this issue. The blueprint should not be authored before the index schema and strata decisions land, because both change what the components actually build.

Sequence: /spec feature blueprint -> /groom-feature-blueprint -> /bead-bonanza. Run /retro-spec and /retro-skill after each phase, which now file to rfcs/inbox/<spec-type>/ and rfcs/inbox/<skill-name>/.
acceptance_criteria: An approved feature blueprint, a groomed set of work orders, and beads dispatched by the bonanza

title: ADR: index cache invalidation
description:
Requested directly by the user, 2026-07-31: 'ADR the cache invalidation'.

FRD-spec-validation-cli defines a 'warm index' (a cached index whose inputs are unchanged since it was built) and hangs three latency ACs on it — AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2 and AC-SPEC-009.4 all assume warmth. Nothing decides how warmth is determined or invalidated.

Open questions the ADR must answer: what keys the cache (content hash, mtime, size, git object id); whether configuration changes invalidate the whole cache or a subset; whether the profile version participates in the key (it must, or a rule change silently reuses stale findings); where the cache lives and whether it is gitignored; what happens on a partial invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR fixing the cache key, the invalidation triggers, the on-disk location, and the correctness argument that a stale finding cannot survive a rule change

title: ADR: adopt strata as the single source of truth for schemas and generated types
description:
Requested in PR #4 review of container-spec-cli (2026-07-31): 'Use strata: git@github.com:strata-lang/strata.git'.

Strata models a structure once and generates JSON Schema, Markdown documentation, and Go structs from that one definition. The reviewer wants it used to model: the specs.toml configuration, the frontmatter structure, the JSON artifacts the tool emits, and the structure of errors/findings emitted as JSON.

## Session setup requirement

This session could NOT reach the strata repo. add_repo failed ('cross-tier adds are not supported in v1'), git clone failed on proxy auth, GitHub MCP is scoped to brettcallaghan/agent-plugins, and WebFetch of raw content 404d. list_repos confirmed the repo IS available to the account (private, can_push).

**Create the next session with BOTH brettcallaghan/agent-plugins AND strata-lang/strata as initial sources.** Without that the ADR cannot be written against the real tool.

## Reading list (from the strata repo root)
- docs/public/strata.llm.md
- docs/content/docs/lang.mdx

## Known constraints
- Do not use the binary from the last release; build the CLI from source (Rust). This is a temporary Rust build-time dependency in a Go project, which the ADR must address.
- Known issue: strata-generated Go structs carry no YAML or TOML tags. The agreed workaround is to convert YAML/TOML to JSON and deserialize from JSON. module-document-core's Frontmatter component already documents this two-step model.
- Strata is a build-time tool whose generated artifacts get committed; advised against embedding strata binaries in this repo (423 KiB packed, distributed by clone via .claude-plugin/marketplace.json).
- Does NOT replace santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema — strata generates the schema, that library validates against it.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR recording the strata adoption decision, what it generates, where generated artifacts live and how they are regenerated, how the Rust build-time dependency is managed in CI, and the YAML/TOML tag workaround

title: ADR: index schema and versioning
description:
The index is the FRD's primary artifact (AC-SPEC-002.2 requires a declared schema version, AC-SPEC-002.3 a workspace identifier so separate repositories' indexes merge). Nothing yet decides the index's actual shape or its versioning policy.

Must resolve the objects-vs-edges question tracked in agent-plugins-dgn, which is architectural input rather than a separate decision. The four sub-decisions listed there are this ADR's agenda.

Interacts with the strata ADR: if strata models the JSON artifacts, the index schema is a strata definition rather than a hand-written JSON Schema.
acceptance_criteria: An approved ADR fixing the index object model, the edge/reference representation, the schema-version scheme, and the cross-repository merge semantics

title: Repo has no CI — zero automated enforcement of its own gates
description:
There is no .github/workflows directory. scripts/check-skills.sh and scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exist and are runnable but nothing runs them on push or PR.

skill-authoring-standards states: 'Every invariant a skill asserts about itself SHALL be enforced by an automated check' with 'Status in this repository: not yet met.' The scripts are half of that; the trigger is missing.

Blocked-adjacent to the spec-validation CLI work (docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md) but should not wait for it — wiring the two existing scripts into a workflow is independently valuable and is the harness the CLI will slot into.
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub Actions workflow runs check-skills.sh --strict and sync-shared-references.sh --check on push and pull_request; a deliberately broken SKILL.md fails the build
close_reason: Added .github/workflows/checks.yml running check-skills.sh and sync-shared-references.sh --check on push and pull_request. --strict deferred to agent-plugins-9ko.

title: ADR slugs don't match how ADRs are cited — 26 dangling wikilinks
description:
11 of 13 ADR files carry a descriptive slug (e.g. slug: adr-011-targeted-verification-gates) while every citation in the repo uses the bare number ([[adr-011]]). template-authoring-standards.md prefix registry says the ADR slug form is adr-<nnn>, so the slugs are wrong, not the links. Only adr-012 and adr-013 conform.

Found by prototyping a link validator over the repo (see docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md). 26 references dangle today: adr-004 x6, adr-005 x5, adr-006 x4, adr-007 x7, adr-008 x3, adr-011 x1 (after excluding code spans and template placeholders).

Fix: change the 11 non-conforming frontmatter slugs to the bare adr-<nnn> form. Filenames stay descriptive — the slug is independent of the filename (standards-template.md v1.2).
acceptance_criteria: Every ADR frontmatter slug matches ^adr-[0-9]{3}$; zero dangling [[adr-*]] references across docs/, rfcs/, plugin/

title: spec: add a type-independent document self-check step (RFC P1)
description:
## Retro

Implemented in the bead-bonanza orchestrator's own loop (no `Agent` tool
exists in this session, so no subagent could be dispatched).

**Changed**

- `plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md` — new
  (102 lines, carries `## Contents`). Eight type-independent checks.
  Checks 1, 2, 3 and 6 cite `[[template-authoring-standards]]`
  (check 3 routing on to `[[frontmatter-standards]]` for the status
  vocabulary); check 8 cites `[[cross-document-references]]`. Checks 4
  (EARS coverage), 5 (compound modal verbs) and 7 (instruction blocks
  deleted) are stated in the file's own voice.
- `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` — new Authoring Workflow step 7
  ("Self-check the finished document"), inserted after step 6
  ("Preflight feature blueprints") and before the retro offer, which
  renumbered from 7 to 8. Frontmatter `version` 1.3 -> 1.4.
- `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — version 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0.

**Implicit decisions made**

- Step number: the new step is 7, retro offer renumbered to 8. No other
  file references the spec skill's step numbers (grepped), so nothing
  downstream needed updating.
- New file's frontmatter: `status: active`, `version: "0.1"`, slug
  `document-readiness-checklist` — matched to its sibling
  `blueprint-readiness-checklist.md`, whose slug likewise ends in
  "checklist" rather than a standards role noun.
- Considered and reverted: a References-table row pointing at the new
  checklist. Every row in that table exceeds 80 columns (table cells are
  exempt from the width rule), but this bead's acceptance criteria state
  an unconditional "every line added or changed is at most 80
  characters". The AC won; the row was removed. The step body cites
  `references/document-readiness-checklist.md` as a backticked path, so
  check-skills.sh still validates the one-hop reference.

**Constraint honored**

`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md` is
byte-identical to its pre-change state (`git diff` empty).

**Gates**

- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` — PASS (11 vendored
  references current; the new file is not a vendored reference).
- `scripts/dogfood-install.sh` — re-materialized `.claude/skills/`.
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — PASS, exit 0. One pre-existing warning
  (bead-bonanza SKILL.md body is 770 lines), unrelated to this bead.
- 80-column check on every added/changed line — clean.

**Not done (forced by the orchestrator's no-commit rule)**

No commit, no push. `scripts/bb-close-bead.sh` was deliberately not used
because it commits; the close, export and stage steps were performed
manually in the skill's prescribed order.
design:
Two edits, both under `plugin/skills/spec/`.

(a) Insert a new numbered step into the Authoring Workflow — the ordered
list beginning at `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:188` — placed after the
existing step 6 ("Preflight feature blueprints", line 210) and before
step 7's retro offer, renumbering the following steps:

    N. **Self-check the finished document.** Before setting any document
       to `ready-for-review`, run
       `references/document-readiness-checklist.md` against it. Fix what
       it reports and re-run; do not set `ready-for-review` while any
       check fails. (Feature blueprints additionally run the blueprint
       readiness checklist in step 6 — that one is about groomability,
       this one about conformance.)

(b) Create `plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md`
holding these eight type-independent checks:

    1. Frontmatter parses as YAML and declares title, description, slug,
       type, status, updated_at.
    2. The slug matches the registry's rule for this type.
    3. status is a value from the controlled vocabulary.
    4. Every normative statement uses an EARS pattern.
    5. No requirement joins two modal verbs with "and".
    6. No prose line exceeds 80 characters (tables, URLs, fences exempt).
    7. Every template instruction comment block has been deleted.
    8. Every [[slug]] reference resolves to an existing document.

CITE, DO NOT RESTATE — this is the triage refinement; do not copy the
RFC's literal checklist text. Checks 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 restate rules the
framework already owns, and the framework forbids duplication
(`plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:205-206`: "Cross-reference other documents
instead of duplicating their content — duplication drifts"). Their
existing homes, verified during triage:

  - `plugin/skills/spec/references/template-authoring-standards.md`
    v0.12 — "### Line Length" (line 42) owns check 6; "## Metadata
    (Frontmatter)" (line 54) owns check 1; "## Slug Conventions"
    (line 62 onward) owns check 2; "### Reference Validation"
    (line 433) owns check 8.
  - `plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md` — owns
    how a `[[slug]]` reference resolves (check 8).

So the new checklist SHALL cite those documents by `[[slug]]` for checks
1/2/3/6/8, and state in its own voice only what is genuinely new:
check 4 (EARS coverage), check 5 (compound modal verbs), check 7
(instruction blocks deleted).

The pattern to follow is stated by the sibling checklist at
`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md:27`:
"The checks are defined only here — the skills reference this document
rather than restating it, so authoring and grooming can never disagree
about what 'groomable' means."

New-file frontmatter must satisfy template-authoring-standards: title,
description, slug, type: standards, status, updated_at, version.

Gate to respect: `scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136` fails any file under
`plugin/skills/*/references/` that exceeds 100 lines without a line
matching `^#+ Contents` or `^Sections \(complete`. Keep the new file
under 100 lines, or give it a `## Contents` section.

Version bumps:
  - `plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md` frontmatter `version: "1.3"` -> "1.4"
    (MINOR).
  - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` "0.7.0" -> "0.8.0" (MINOR).
    Shared with agent-plugins-8bx and agent-plugins-x8t — set the value
    idempotently; do not bump a second time if it already reads 0.8.0.

CONSTRAINT: do not weaken or widen
`plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md`. It
gates groomability, which is a separate concern, and the source RFC
lists leaving it alone as an explicit Non-Goal.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A new numbered step exists in the Authoring Workflow of
      plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md, positioned after "Preflight feature
      blueprints" and before the retro-offer step, and its wording
      applies to every document type rather than to feature blueprints
      only.
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md
      exists and covers all eight checks listed in Design.
- [ ] For checks 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 the new file cites
      [[template-authoring-standards]] / [[cross-document-references]]
      instead of restating their rules; checks 4, 5 and 7 are stated in
      the new file's own voice.
- [ ] The new file is under 100 lines, or carries a "## Contents"
      section.
- [ ] The new file's frontmatter declares title, description, slug,
      type: standards, status, updated_at and version.
- [ ] Every line added or changed in every touched file is at most 80
      characters.
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md frontmatter version reads "1.4".
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version reads "0.8.0".
- [ ] plugin/skills/spec/references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md is
      byte-identical to its pre-change state.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: authors a NEW normative framework document plus a workflow step that gates every document type; must judge which of 8 checks to cite vs. state in its own voice across two other standards docs, and a restating checklist would create exactly the duplication-drift the framework forbids. Well-specified but invention-heavy with framework-wide blast radius.

title: triage-rfc: rule for versioning a changed file that has no version property (RFC P2)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 5 instructs the agent to bump versions, and every
verb presupposes a predecessor. It gives no rule for a changed file
that carries no version property at all.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:182-190`:

    - Bump the version of every changed template (instruction-block
      `Version:`), skill (frontmatter `version`), and standard
      (frontmatter `version`) per [[template-authoring-standards]].
      **Bump each file exactly once for the whole triage, no matter how
      many proposals changed it** — ...

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

`plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`plugin/skills/spec/references/ears-guide.md` had no `version` field —
the absence was itself one of the things that run was fixing. With no
rule available, the agent wrote `version: "0.2"` into `c4-guide.md`,
reasoning that the file was also receiving a content change and so
should land above its initial value, then reversed itself in a second
edit within the same run to `version: "0.1"`, on the ground that `0.2`
implies a `0.1` that a reader could diff against and none ever existed.
Both guides shipped `0.1`. The reversal is two consecutive edits to one
line in that session.

This is not cosmetic. Step 1's provenance check is version-keyed
(SKILL.md:66-67: "compare the cited skill/template/standard versions
against the current ones"), so a version implying a predecessor that
never existed makes the "already fixed?" question unanswerable for that
file.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P2 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Append to the version-bump bullet in step 5, after the existing
sentence ending "verify the bump after the final change to that file,
never before.", continuing the same 5-space bullet-body indentation:

     WHEN a changed file carries no version property at all, do not
     bump — add one at `0.1`, and let this triage's change land inside
     that first version. A higher initial value implies a predecessor a
     reader could diff against; for a file that has never been
     versioned there is none, and step 1's provenance check would then
     be asking about a version that never existed. Place the property
     per [[frontmatter-standards]].

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The step-5 version bullet states that a file with no version property gets 0.1 rather than a bump
- [ ] It gives the reason (a higher initial value implies a predecessor that never existed)
- [ ] It points at [[frontmatter-standards]] for placement
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: a single append to the end of one existing bullet with the wording supplied; no other step references it and no cross-file coordination is needed. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: Step 5 version bullet now covers a changed file with no version property (add 0.1, do not bump).

metadata.tier_reason: single append to the end of one existing bullet with wording supplied; no other step references it

title: triage-rfc: admit triage-originated changes to step 4 and the Resolution (RFC P3)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 4 and the Resolution format both assume every change
originates as a proposal in a received RFC, so a change triage itself
originates has no id, no table row and no outcome slot.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:127-128`:

    4. **Present the recommendation and STOP for approval.** One table:
       proposal, classification, one-line rationale, files touched.

`SKILL.md:225-228` (the Resolution bullet) is likewise per-proposal:
"per-proposal outcome (adopted / adopted-with-refinement + the
refinement / deferred + bead id / rejected + rationale)".

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

That run adopted one change no RFC proposed: adding a `version`
property to `plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`ears-guide.md`. It was not a proposal — both RFCs had recorded it
under *Considered and Not Proposed*, RFC 0007 explicitly asking for "a
sweep of all guides rather than two one-line fixes".

With no rule to follow, the agent invented a row id `X1` outside the
`P` numbering, annotated it "(your call — not a proposal)", and then at
Resolution time invented a section heading "**Also adopted, outside
this RFC's proposals**" because no per-proposal row could hold it. Two
inventions in one run for one change.

The same gap recurred immediately: the following triage run took a
change reported directly by the human (see the sibling bead on the
already-implemented wording), which likewise had no id or row until one
was improvised.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P3 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Two edits.

1. In step 4, immediately after the sentence "One table: proposal,
   classification, one-line rationale, files touched." and before
   "Implement nothing before the human approves", insert at 3-space
   indent:

   A triage MAY originate a change no RFC proposed — one the evidence
   implies, or an item an RFC recorded under Considered and Not
   Proposed that this triage judges ready. Table it as its own row,
   numbered `T1..Tn` so it is never confused with an RFC's `P` ids,
   with its origin given as triage. It carries the same evidence bar
   and needs the same approval; what it lacks is a reporter, so the
   rationale column carries triage's own reasoning and says so.

2. Append to the Resolution bullet in step 5 (the bullet beginning
   "Write the RFC's Resolution section"), continuing its indentation:

     Record any `T` change in the Resolution of the RFC whose evidence
     prompted it, in its own row, marked as triage-originated rather
     than that RFC's testimony. WHERE no RFC prompted it — a change
     reported directly by the human — record it in the Resolution of
     the RFC triaged alongside it, marked the same way.

The second sentence of edit 2 goes beyond the RFC's proposed wording:
the RFC assumed a T change always traces to some RFC's evidence, and
the run that filed this bead produced one that did not. Flag this as an
adopted-with-refinement in the Resolution.

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 4 describes triage-originated rows and the T1..Tn numbering
- [ ] Step 4 states they need the same approval and the same evidence bar
- [ ] The Resolution bullet says where a T change is recorded, including when no RFC prompted it
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead

title: triage-rfc: make already-implemented vs reject-already-addressed distinguishable (triage T1)
description:
## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:120-126` defines the
`already-implemented` classification and distinguishes it from
`reject — already addressed` with a single clause: "which is for a
proposal whose premise no longer holds". A human reader of the skill
reported that this does not convey the distinction, because in BOTH
cases the change is already present in the tree, so "the premise no
longer holds" appears to describe both.

Current text at SKILL.md:120-126:

    - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
      already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
      this triage. Distinct from `reject — already addressed`, which is
      for a proposal whose premise no longer holds: this one was right
      and nothing about it is being turned down. Record it in the
      Resolution as "adopted — already implemented", name where the
      change lives, and bump nothing.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Reported directly by the repository owner on 2026-08-01, quoting
SKILL.md:122 and stating: "This does not make it clear (to me) what the
distinction between `reject - already addressed` and `adopted - already
implemented`."

This is a triage-originated work order (id T1), not a proposal from a
received RFC. It has no reporting RFC; the reporter is the human gate.

The distinction that the text should convey, and currently does not:
both outcomes mean the change is already in the tree, but they differ
in whether triage is ruling on the proposal's MERITS at all.
`adopted — already implemented` affirms the proposal was correct;
`reject — already addressed` takes no position, because the thing the
proposal targeted no longer exists. The consequence is load-bearing at
step 2, which reads prior Resolutions during dedupe: "adopted" means
settled, do not relitigate; "rejected — already addressed" means only
that the evidence was stale, so the same idea with fresh evidence gets
a fresh hearing.
design:
Replace the `already-implemented` bullet at SKILL.md:120-126 with:

   - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
     already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
     this triage. Record it in the Resolution as "adopted — already
     implemented", name where the change lives, and bump nothing.

     The test against `reject — already addressed` is whether triage is
     ruling on the proposal's merits at all. Use **already-implemented**
     WHEN you would have adopted it had the tree been untouched: the
     proposal was right, and this triage says so. Use **reject —
     already addressed** WHEN there is nothing to rule on — the text it
     quotes is gone or rewritten, so its premise fails and triage takes
     no position on whether the idea was ever good.

     The difference is load-bearing at step 2, which reads prior
     Resolutions. "Adopted" tells a future triage the idea is settled
     and should not be relitigated; "rejected — already addressed"
     tells it only that the evidence was stale, so the same idea backed
     by fresh evidence gets a fresh hearing.

Keep the bullet in place in step 3's list; do not reorder the
classifications. Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The already-implemented bullet states the merits test (would you have adopted it had the tree been untouched)
- [ ] It states what reject — already addressed means instead (nothing to rule on; premise fails)
- [ ] It names the step-2 dedupe consequence for both outcomes
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: a single self-contained bullet replacement with the full text supplied and no interaction with other steps; the only judgment is preserving list indentation. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: already-implemented bullet now states the merits test, what reject-already-addressed means instead, and the step-2 dedupe consequence for both.

title: No merge strategy for .beads/issues.jsonl — beads created on two branches will conflict
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is the only carrier of issues between sessions and branches in this project (see the 'How beads persist in THIS project' section of CLAUDE.md). There is no `.gitattributes` in the repo, so git merges it as ordinary text.

Two branches that each create beads produce overlapping line-level edits in one file. Git will report a conflict, and the natural resolutions are both wrong: taking one side drops the other branch's issues, and a careless union can duplicate ids or interleave a partial record.

The failure is silent in the worst case — a conflict resolved by 'keep mine' loses issues that were correctly exported and committed, which is exactly the loss the export discipline exists to prevent.

## Options to evaluate
- A `.gitattributes` union merge driver for the file. Cheap, but union can produce two lines with the same id when both branches touched one issue, so it needs an id-dedupe pass afterwards.
- A custom merge driver that parses JSONL, keys by id, and prefers the higher `updated_at`. Correct, but needs a script every clone can run.
- Regenerate from the database after merge rather than merging the file: resolve by taking either side, then `bd import` both versions and `bd export` fresh. Uses beads' own conflict handling.
- Whether beads upstream ships a documented driver for this — check before building one.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested procedure for merging two branches that both added beads, with no issue lost and no duplicate id in the resulting .beads/issues.jsonl

title: Index: model references as a separate edge collection, not only object properties
description:
Architectural input for the index-schema ADR (not yet written). Raised in PR #4 review of the FRD, 2026-07-31, explicitly flagged as 'not a comment for the FRD, but an architectural one for later'.

## The proposal

The index should collect the domain's model objects — specs
('documents'), systems, containers, components, and eventually features
— AND separately build a collection of REFERENCES that behave like
edges in a graph rather than like members of the objects they connect.
Each reference carries the file and span where it occurs.

Rationale given: this makes references queryable independently of the
objects. 'What points at adr-007?' becomes an edge query rather than a
scan over every object's properties.

This does not mean relationships never live inside objects. Some
belong there — a 'component' object might carry an injected
'container' property naming its parent. The proposal is specifically
about references that occur INSIDE document bodies: those are better
modelled as edges.

## Why it is not in the FRD

The FRD (docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md) states WHAT the index
must contain, and AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 already require
outbound and inbound references. HOW the index is shaped — one
collection of objects with embedded arrays, versus objects plus a
separate edge collection — is a schema design decision, and the FRD
deliberately defers index schema and versioning to an ADR.

## Why it matters more than it looks

AC-SPEC-002.2 makes the index schema a published API with a version
identifier, and AC-SPEC-002.3 requires a workspace identifier so
indexes from separate repositories merge into one graph. An edge
collection is materially easier to merge across repositories than
embedded arrays, because edges from repo A pointing at objects in repo
B are just rows — whereas embedded arrays require rewriting the source
object. Getting this wrong is expensive to change after publication.

## Related decisions already made

- Reference relationships are DERIVED from body wikilinks, not
  hand-maintained frontmatter (settled in review; see
  docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md section 3).
- A 'span' carries a byte offset and length plus line/column, so an
  edge can record exactly where in the source the reference occurs
  (FRD Terminology, revised 2026-07-31).
design:
Input to the index-schema ADR; not standalone work. The ADR must decide:

1. Objects-with-embedded-arrays vs objects-plus-edge-collection vs both.
2. IF both, which relationships live where, and how duplication between
   the two representations is prevented from drifting.
3. Whether edges are typed (references / parent / supersedes / composes)
   or uniform with a 'kind' discriminator.
4. How edges behave across a workspace boundary when the target object
   is not in this repository's index.

Do not implement ahead of that ADR — the index schema is a published
API under AC-SPEC-002.2 and changing it later is the expensive case.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The index-schema ADR records a decision on object-vs-edge representation, with this proposal weighed in Alternatives Considered.
- [ ] The decision addresses cross-repository merge, since that is the case that most distinguishes the options.
- [ ] IF edges are adopted, the FRD's AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 are re-examined for consistency with the chosen shape.

title: triage-rfc: should the sequencing escape hatch key on the graph's consumer? (RFC P4)
description:
DEFERRED at triage on 2026-08-01. Not dispatchable as written — the
evidence is self-referential and one more independent observation is
wanted before the rule is changed. Status is 'deferred' so it stays out
of 'bd ready'.

## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:173-175` gives the escape hatch
from the sequencing rule:

    WHERE the approved set is small and touches disjoint files,
    implement inline and say so; grooming a two-file change is
    overhead.

The hatch turns on the SHAPE of the approved set — size and file
disjointness. The variable that has actually decided the question in
practice is different: whether anything will CONSUME the dependency
graph that grooming produces. A single agent implementing inline, with
no dispatch and no parallelism, produces a graph with no reader.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Two observations, both from model claude-opus-5, both in the session of
2026-08-01, and both made by the agent that authored the rule.

1. The triage that ADOPTED this rule (RFC 0008 P1) then declined to
   follow it. Its approved set was 10 proposals with 6 colliding on one
   file — neither small nor disjoint, so the hatch did not apply and
   the rule required filing 10 beads and running `groom-beads`. The
   agent implemented inline and recorded the deviation in
   `rfcs/rfc-0008-triage-rfc-implementation-sequencing.md` under
   Resolution. Its stated reason was the missing consumer, not the set
   shape. Correctness the rule protects — serialized edits to a shared
   file, version bump last — was obtained by hand and verified.

2. The next triage run hit the same fork: 5 approved changes plus one
   human-reported change, all landing on the same file. The human was
   asked to choose and directed that the rule be followed, which is how
   the beads for that run (including this one) came to exist.

## Why this was deferred rather than adopted

Both observations are the same agent in the same session, so this is
repetition rather than independent corroboration. The RFC proposing it
says so itself: "Triage may reasonably defer it for corroboration from
a run that did not author it."

The cost of deferring is real and should be weighed on any future
recurrence: the rule stays miscalibrated, and the next single-agent
triage either files beads nobody reads or deviates again.

## What would make this ready

Any ONE of:
- A triage run under a different model, or in a different session,
  hitting the same fork and recording what it did.
- A decision that filing the graph is worth it regardless of consumer
  (e.g. because the beads are themselves the audit record) — which
  would close this by rejecting it, not by adopting it.

## The proposed change, if it is ever adopted

Replace SKILL.md:173-175 with:

     WHERE the approved set is small and touches disjoint files, OR
     WHERE the implementation will run in a single agent with no
     dispatch and no parallelism, implement inline and say so —
     sequencing the colliding edits by hand and bumping each file after
     its last change, which is what the graph would have enforced. File
     the graph when something will consume it: parallel agents, a
     `bead-bonanza` run, or work resuming in a later session. A graph
     with no reader is filing, not sequencing.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P4 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 2 as of the
second observation above).
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: if it ever becomes ready the edit is a single bullet replacement with the wording already drafted; the difficulty is entirely in the decision, not the execution. No C4 component is affected. grooming_status: blocked-needs-info — the missing fact is one observation from a run that did not author the rule.

title: bd auto-export does not propagate deletions to issues.jsonl
description:
Measured 2026-07-31 in this repo, bd 1.1.2, with `export.auto: true` and `interval: 60s` in .beads/config.yaml.

Creating an issue refreshed .beads/issues.jsonl immediately (10 lines to 19). `bd delete` on that same issue did NOT: the deleted record was still in the file after 90 seconds, well past the interval. Only an explicit `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl` produced a correct file (18 lines, probe absent).

Consequence in this project: because the SessionStart hook rebuilds the database by importing that file, a deleted issue silently comes back in the next session.

Worked around by documenting the explicit export in the session-close steps in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Worth reporting upstream, and worth re-testing on a bd upgrade — if auto export becomes authoritative the manual step can go.
acceptance_criteria: Either upstream fixes it and the manual export step is removed from CLAUDE.md, or the limitation is confirmed as intended and the workaround stays with a link to the upstream decision
notes: Follow-up test 2026-07-31: the beads PRE-COMMIT hook uses the same append/update path, so it does not rescue a deletion either. Sequence: create probe -> commit (file gains it, 21 lines) -> bd delete probe -> commit again (file STILL has it, 21 lines). An earlier commit that printed 'Exported 20 issues' and produced a correct file was correct only because an explicit bd export had been run moments before. Conclusion: an explicit 'bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl' is the only form that reflects deletions.

title: frontmatter: can 'sources' record an input that is not a spec document? (RFC 0006 P4)
description:
DEFERRED at triage on 2026-07-31. Not dispatchable as written — the scope decision below is unmade. Status is 'deferred' so it stays out of 'bd ready'.

## Problem

A 'sources' frontmatter property is defined as holding SLUGS ONLY:
'plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md:119' declares
'sources: []   # Source document slugs'. The FRD template repeats it at
'plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md:8' — 'slugs of documents
this FRD is based on'.

But documents outside the specification set have no slug BY DESIGN.
'plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md:124-125'
states: 'The [[document-slug]] notation SHALL be reserved for documents
in the specification set; it SHALL NOT be used for documents outside
it.' Research briefs, vendor docs and prior-art reviews are correctly
out-of-set and correctly slugless.

So an FRD derived from an out-of-set input cannot record that fact.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

'docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md' was derived almost entirely from
'docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md', a ~700-line research brief
carrying prototype measurements and nine resolved scope questions. The
brief is correctly not a spec document and correctly has no slug. The
FRD therefore ships with 'sources: []' — which is FALSE. Its only record
of provenance is one backticked path in the References prose section.

The index specified by that same FRD (REQ-SPEC-002) would report the
document as having no sources at all.

## Why this was deferred rather than adopted

The RFC proposed changing 'frd-template.md:8' alone. Triage rejected
that scope: 'frontmatter-standards.md' OWNS the property, so changing
one template alone would make a template contradict its standard — which
is precisely the defect class P1 of the same RFC was adopted to remove
(the ADR template contradicting the prefix registry, which produced 11
non-conforming slugs and 26 dangling references).

Three templates carry a 'sources' property:
  plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md
  plugin/skills/spec/references/feature-blueprint-template.md
  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md

## What must be decided before this is groomable

1. Should 'sources' accept a mixed list (slugs for in-set documents,
   repo-relative paths for out-of-set ones), or should a SECOND property
   carry out-of-set inputs? A mixed list keeps one property but makes
   every consumer discriminate two value shapes; a second property keeps
   each shape clean but adds vocabulary to a deliberately small set.
2. Whichever is chosen, 'frontmatter-standards.md' changes FIRST as the
   owner, then the three templates follow in the same change.
3. Does the same treatment apply to 'related', which has the identical
   slugs-only constraint?

Source: rfcs/rfc-0006-spec-reference-bundles-and-adr-slug.md, proposal
P4. Retro that produced it: rfcs/retro-note-frd-authoring-2026-07-31.md
design:
NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — the three questions above are unmade decisions. A grooming pass can only start once a human picks (1) and confirms (3).

Whichever shape wins, the change ORDER is fixed: frontmatter-standards.md (the owner) first, then frd-template.md, feature-blueprint-template.md and work-order-template.md in the same commit, each with its instruction-block Version bumped, plus the plugin version. Landing a template ahead of the standard reproduces the exact contradiction P1 was adopted to remove.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A human has chosen mixed-list vs second-property, and answered whether 'related' gets the same treatment.
- [ ] frontmatter-standards.md defines the chosen form, and its version is bumped.
- [ ] All three templates carrying 'sources' match that definition, each with its instruction-block Version bumped.
- [ ] No template states a rule about 'sources' that frontmatter-standards.md does not.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

title: templates: placeholder section lists convey nothing (RFC P4)
description:
GROOMING OUTCOME: blocked-ungroomable. NOT dispatchable. Do not hand
this bead to an implementing agent — the change it describes is defective
as written and its scope is undecided. See "Why this is blocked" below
and the reshape requirements in Design. Status is `deferred` so it stays
out of `bd ready`.

Source: `rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md`, proposal P4
(severity polish, origin self, runs_observed 1, model claude-opus-5).
Filed by an RFC triage pass that stopped at step 4 on human instruction;
nothing was implemented. The triage recommendation was DEFER.

PROBLEM AS REPORTED
`plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md:15-18` reads:

    Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction block)
      - <Major Category>
      - <Another Major Category>
      - References

For a template whose sections are author-defined, this enumerates
placeholders and conveys little. It contrasts with the fixed-section
templates — ADR (Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered /
Consequences / References) — where the same list is a genuine map.
The RFC proposes replacing the placeholder list with a structural note:
"Structure: one `##` per major requirement category, `###` per
subcategory, then a References section. Categories are author-defined;
name them for the domain, not for this template."

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED (three findings, all verified during grooming)

1. The proposed change breaks the repo's own gate.
   `scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136` fails any file under
   `plugin/skills/*/references/` longer than 100 lines that has no line
   matching `^#+ Contents` or `^Sections \(complete`:

       for p in glob.glob('plugin/skills/*/references/*.md'):
           if '/shared/' in p: continue
           t = open(p).read()
           if len(t.split('\n')) > 100 and not re.search(
                   r'^#+ Contents|^Sections \(complete', t, re.M):
               err(p, "over 100 lines with no table of contents")

   `standards-template.md` is 218 lines and clears that gate only via
   its line 15, "Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction
   block)" — the exact line P4 deletes. The RFC's replacement text
   matches neither alternation branch, so applying P4 verbatim makes
   `scripts/check-skills.sh` fail on the very file it edits.

2. The real scope is ten files, and the RFC specifies one.
   Ten templates under `plugin/skills/spec/references/` carry the same
   "Sections (complete each" construct — verified by grep: adr,
   component-blueprint, container-blueprint, contract, feature-blueprint,
   frd, module-blueprint, standards, system-blueprint, work-order. The
   RFC addresses only the author-defined-section case and does not say
   which of the ten keep their enumerated list. A dispatched agent would
   have to invent that taxonomy decision.

3. No run cost, so nothing forces the call now. The RFC's own
   justification is "worth doing while the section lists are being
   reviewed for other reasons" — it records no evidence that the
   placeholder list harmed a run.
design:
NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. This bead is blocked-ungroomable; what
follows is what a human must decide before it can be re-groomed, and
what a reshaped change would have to satisfy.

UNBLOCK CRITERIA (any implementing work needs all three settled)

A. A human adopt/defer decision. The current recommendation is DEFER,
   pending a second, independent project reporting the same friction —
   at which point the `theme:template-ergonomics` label makes the
   recurrence countable.

B. A scope decision naming, of the ten templates carrying the
   "Sections (complete each" construct (adr, component-blueprint,
   container-blueprint, contract, feature-blueprint, frd,
   module-blueprint, standards, system-blueprint, work-order), which
   are in scope for the structural note and which keep their enumerated
   list. The RFC treats this as a one-file edit; it is not.

C. A gate strategy, picking exactly one of:
   - keep a line matching `^Sections \(complete` in every touched file
     over 100 lines; or
   - add a `## Contents` heading to every touched file over 100 lines;
     or
   - deliberately amend the regex at `scripts/check-skills.sh:135` to
     accept the new form, as its own reviewed change.

A reshaped bead would also have to bump each touched template's
instruction-block `Version`, plus
`plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

WHY NOT blocked-needs-info: the block is not one missing fact. Even
given a human "adopt", the change still needs redesign (B and C), so
this is a redesign block, not an information block.
